column3: Description
column18: Comment

column3: Aggregates the product's circular-economy performance into one score by combining the five level-2 circular indicators: reclamation efficiency (C1), process quality and performance (C2), design for circularity (C3), the circular flow index (C4) and circular end-of-life handling (C5). Covers the implementation and process of circular (R-strategy) principles only; it excludes social, cost, environmental and efficiency aspects, which are scored in their own domains.
column4: To provide a view of current circular initiatives and locate potential improvement points.
column9: Sum (weight * C1 + weight * C2 + weight * C3 + weight * C4 + weight * C5)

column3: Aggregates how effective the product's return and reclamation processes are, combining the reclaimed-packaging rate (C11), the end-of-life product take-back rate (C12), and the recovery yield of the reclaimed products (C13). Indicates how much of what is sold returns and how usefully it is recovered.
column4: To assess the effectiveness of the reclamation method / program.
column18: SASB has no direct reclamation-rate metric (RT-CP-250a.1 is chemicals-of-concern; RT-CP-410a.2 is revenue-based) — dropped SASB RT-250a.1 as off-topic.

column3: Measures the share of returned packaging. Normalized through the expected or target number of reclaimed packaging.
column4: To reduce virgin packaging use and remove potential waste.
column9: Reclaimed = Reclaimed packaging material weight / Total Sold Packaging Weight\n\n(Reclaimed - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).\nWeight-based, packaging-only adaptation of GRI 301-3 (which is count-based over products sold and combines products + packaging).

column3: Measures the share of returned products  after the expected use time. An existing program such as take-back policies must exist. Does NOT include recalls and rejects. The focus is to reclaim products that have fulfilled their use purpose.
column4: To increase product take-back rates. Ensure materials and components re-enter the value chain.
column9: Reclaimed = Number of reclaimed product / Number of units sold\n\n(Reclaimed - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Measures the proportion of material or components that can be effectively reused, refurbished, or recycled from the EoL reclamations. Due to various reasons, not 100% of the reclaimed product could be used.
column4: To assess the overall quality of product components at its EoL and to improve current recovery pipeline.
column9: Recovered = Weight of valuable unit components / Weight of Reclaimed Units\n\n(Recovered - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Total number of units sold to customers.
Total number of units reclaimed from their EoL.
Total amount of packaging of unit reclaimed after the purchase.
Total weight of packaging materials sold to customer.
Total weight of units reclaimed from their EoL.
Total weight of valuable components recovered from the overall reclaimed units. The rest of the non-valuable components will be used for scrap.

Aggregates the product's circular-process performance into one score by combining the refurbishment (C21), repair (C22), and remanufacturing (C23) process sub-scores. Provides an overview of all circular processes to locate potential improvements.
column4: To provide a view of all circular processes for potential improvements.
column9: Sum (weight * C21 + weight * C22 + weight * C23)

column3: Measures the overall effectiveness of the refurbishment processes, focusing on the ability to restore products to a saleable condition.
column4: To provide a view of refurbishment processes for potential improvements.
column18: Refurbishment here = restore-to-resalable; DIN SPEC 91472 §3.6 defines refurbishment as not placed on the market — product-level adaptation.

column3: Measures the rate at which products that pass the refurbishment process. Ideally all incoming products should pass the refurbishment process, not all units can be restored to a sellable or usable condition due to varying issues.
column4: To monitor and increase the yield of refurbishment pipeline.
column9: Success = Number of successful refurbished products / Number of processed products intake for refurbishment\n\n(Success - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Measures the test performance of refurbished products against new products. Depends highly on its testing standards. Applicable to companies with an established testing process. Ideally achieves the same or better test results as new-products.
column4: To ensure products meet company standards and warranty targets.
column9: Quality = Avg(test results of refurbished) / Avg(test results of new-products)\n\n(Quality - Min) / (Max - Min)

column3: Measures the time taken to produce one unit of product from start to finish compared to planned time.
column4: To reduce cycle times and improve time-to-resale.

column2: Number of Units assigned for Refurbishment
column3: Number of units put into the refurbishment process.
Number of units passing the refurbishment quality check.
The result of refurbished units after undergoing performance and quality testing.
The result of new units after undergoing performance and quality testing.
Time taken to finish the refurbishment of a unit.
Measures the efficiency and effectiveness of repair operations of the product.
column4: To provide a view to prioritize improvements in repair quality, speed and longevity.

column3: Measures the rate at which products that pass the repair process. Ideally all incoming products should pass the repair process. Gives overall overview on the effectiveness of current repair processes.
column4: To monitor and increase the yield of repair pipeline and reduce repair iteration.
column9: Success = Number of Successful Repaired Units / Number of Units assigned for Repair\n\n(Success - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Measures the additional lifespan a product achieves after undergoing repairs. It assesses how effectively repairs can prolong the usability of products.
column4: To ensure repairs restore lasting value and minimize repeating repairs / warranty costs.
column9: Longevity = Lifespan of Repaired Units / Original Lifespan of Units\n\n(Longevity - Min) / (Max - Min)

column3: Measures the punctuality of repaired products.
column4: To reduce customer waiting time and improve throughput.

column3: Number of units put into the repairment process.
Number of units passing the repair quality check.
The duration for which a product remains functional and usable after it has been repaired.
The estimated or documented time period for which a product remains functional after purchase.
Time taken to finish the repairment of a unit.

Aggregates the remanufacturing process into one score by combining the remanufactured-component share (C231), the restored-component share (C232), and the remanufacture success rate (C233). Reflects the ability to restore used products to at least new-equivalent quality while maximizing reuse of secondary components.
column4: To provide a view of remanufacturing quality, circularity, and value recovery to guide pipeline improvements.
column9: Sum (weight * C231 + weight * C232 + weight * C233)

column3: Measures the share of a remanufactured unit's components that are remanufactured (secondary-origin) parts, computed as remanufactured components (C2-13) ÷ total component inflow (C2-11). Higher means a larger fraction of the unit is built from restored/secondary components rather than new ones.
column4: To increase circular material use and reduce reliance on new components.
column9: Ratio = Total components remanufactured (C2-13) / Total components inflow (C2-11)\n\n(Ratio - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Measures the ratio of successfully restored components and the inflow of EoL components set for restoration.
column4: To ensure restoration process effectiveness and maximize reuse of secondary components.
column9: Restored = Total components remanufactured / Total secondary components inflow\n\n(Ratio - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Measures the remanufacturing output volume — the total number of units successfully remanufactured (C2-14) — normalized against a target band. Higher means more units are remanufactured to new-equivalent standard.
column4: To assess the effectiveness of the remanufacturing process.

column3: The total components (both new and secondary) included in the remanufactured product.
column18: Could be components instead, but now in kg for calculation simplicity.

column3: The total components set for quality restoration to the new product standard.
The total components actually integrated into a remanufactured unit.
The total product / unit remanufactured.
Measures the design effort for which the product supports the circular economy principles. This KPI aligns with the R1-R3 principle, where the efforts for a circular product comes from the design.
column4: To guide decisions to maximize circularity in the product design.
column18: The exact circular efforts in practice are not explicitly considered here, but in the "Circular EoL Handling" KPI.

column3: Measures the share of materials that can be recycled after disassembly.
column4: To reduce wasted materials and increase secondary materials generation.
column9: Recyclability = Recyclable Material Weight / Total Product Weight\n\n(Recyclability - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Does not consider whether the materials are recycled in- or out-of-loop. | Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Measures the share of the product's total mass made of components designed to be remanufactured — i.e. restored to at-least-as-new functionality and reused in a new product (remanufacturable component weight ÷ total product weight). Higher means more of the product is designed for value-retaining remanufacturing.
column4: To save more energy in making products by increasing the remanufactured parts from previous EoL products.
column9: Remanufacturability = Remanufacturable Component Weight / Total Product weight\n\n(Remanufacturability - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).\nProduct-level design share of remanufacturable components; remanufacturing concept per DIN SPEC 91472 / ESRS E5; the weight-share formula is author-defined.

column3: Measures the share of components that can be repurposed into other uses. A repurposing pipeline needs to exist.
column4: To enable new value streams and reduce waste through repurposing.
column9: Repurposability = Repurposable Component Weight / Total Product Weight\n\n(Repurposability - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).\nProduct-level design share of repurposable components; repurposing concept per WS+24 / ESRS E5; the weight-share formula is author-defined (WS+24 gives a qualitative attribute basis, not a mass-share metric).

column3: Measures how easily the product can be disassembled at end of life, combining two normalized (0–1) sub-scores: the availability and clarity of disassembly instructions (C3-5) and the product's disassembly time (C3-6, where less time scores better). Higher means lower labour/time to separate components and materials, enabling higher recovery rates.
column4: To reduce labor and time at disassembly and enable higher recovery rates. To simplify and improve separation efforts.

column3: Total weight of a product unit.
Total weight of the recyclable material in the product. Adhering to ISO 14021 specifications.
Total weight of remanufacturable components in the product's design.
Total weight of repurposable components in the product's design.

A normalized (0–1) score for how well disassembly/repair instructions are provided — covering the availability, completeness and clarity of the product manual, exploded views and troubleshooting guidance. Self-normalized against the company's Target Min/Max band; higher means clearer, more complete instructions.
column18: Self-normalizes against company Target Min/Max (0-1 score); for C3-6 lower time is better — set Max=worst-acceptable time. Re-tagged from RAW_VALUE 2026-06 (T3.5).

column3: A normalized (0–1) score derived from the time required to fully disassemble the product (raw input in minutes). Self-normalized against the company's Target Min/Max band, where less disassembly time is better — so the Max is set to the worst-acceptable disassembly time. Higher score means faster, easier disassembly.
column18: Self-normalizes against company Target Min/Max (0-1 score); for C3-6 lower time is better — set Max=worst-acceptable time. Re-tagged from RAW_VALUE 2026-06 (T3.5).

column3: Scores the circularity of the product's material flow as one minus the share of material that flows linearly — i.e. one minus the proportion sourced from virgin resources (C4-1) and ending as unrecoverable waste (C4-2), relative to the total mass flow (C4-3). Higher means a more restorative, less linear material flow. Adapts the Ellen MacArthur Foundation Material Circularity Indicator (Linear Flow Index), without the product-utility factor.
column4: To reduce the proportion of virgin material to unrecoverable waste, which improves circularity.
column9: 1 - (Virgin Material Inflow + Wasted Material Outflow) / (2 * Total Mass Flow)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Total amount of raw materials going in to the process. It includes all materials NOT processed from secondary materials.
column18: Implicitly contains how much recycled materials are used for the product.

column3: Total amount of wasted materials going out of the process. "Wasted" means not further processed for other uses.
Total amount of mass involved in the process either going in OR going out of the system in a closed loop system.
column18: Holds product mass M; C4 applies the ×2 (total mass flow 2M) per MCI Eq. 2.10.

column3: Measures the circular actions in practice for which the product supports the circular economy principles such as the amount of recycled, refurbished, repurposed components.
column4: To provide overview on current circularity actions. The goal is to achieve a 100% handling of EoL products, meaning no parts are wasted.
column9:
(Refurbished product weight + Remanufactured component weight + Repurposed component weight + Recycled component weight) / Total reclaimed units weight

OR

Discarded component weight / Total reclaimed units weight

The quality of reclamation is in another KPI. | Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).\nProduct-level adaptation of ISO 59020 §A.3.3 (Formula A.5) / Figure A.2 outflow-circularity: circular outflow mass ÷ total reclaimed outflow mass; ISO splits reuse/recycle/renewable-recirculation, here grouped as refurbish/remanufacture/repurpose/recycle.

The total component weight sent to the remanufacturing pipeline.
The total component weight sent for repurposing as another product.
